newsitem.title: GERMANY: Europe central bank to focus on open market - Issing.
newsitem.headline: Europe central bank to focus on open market - Issing.

text.p: Bundesbank board member Otmar Issing said the European central bank will focus monetary policy on open market measures.
"Open market policies will be at the centre of the monetary policies of the European central bank," Issing said in a speech at Nuremberg University.

He said Germany's partner nations were in agreement on that, but they were opposed to the Bundesbank's desire to use minimum reserves as a tool to steer the markets. He said whether or not this instrument is used by the European central bank will not be decided before the second half of 1998.
He said Germany's partners had so far only agreed to prepare the way for the use of minimum reserves. It will be up to the European central bank to decide to use that instrument.
Issing said there was little chance that a German-style "discount rate" will be adapted by the European central bank.
"It is not exportable for Europe," he said.
